methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $7.6B.

private.name: Archer Aviation

data.narrative:
Joby Aviation, a public-stage drone and autonomous systems company, is evaluated against a peer set of three same-sector comparables spanning Series G private and public stages: Zipline ($7.6B), Nuro ($6.0B), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B). The broader addressable peer universe in Drones & Autonomous includes seven private companies, with top peers including Elroy Air and Aurora Innovation alongside the three direct comparables.

Peer-median valuation methodology is applicable and yields $6.0B, anchored on the median of the three-company set. This method reflects the valuation range observed across the comparable universe of $3.3B to $7.6B. Given the limited methodological toolkit available from provided data, the peer-median result represents the primary triangulation point for analysis.

The triangulated valuation range supports $5.1B at the low end and $6.9B at the high end, with $6.0B as the central estimate. Joby's current public valuation of $6.86B sits within this range near the upper bound. Key uncertainties include execution risk on commercial deployment timelines, regulatory pathway clarity for advanced air mobility platforms, and capital requirements through certification phases—factors not directly captured in the peer-median approach. The compressed methodological basis (single applicable method) and modest peer sample size limit confidence in precision beyond the $5.1B–$6.9B band.
